instructions: Zotero is the user's reference manager: their library of papers, books and other sources, with PDFs and other files, annotations, notes, collections and tags. Use these tools to find and read the user's sources, cite them in a citation style, add or organize items in their library, import and export them, and show them to the user in Zotero's windows. They work on the Zotero app on the user's computer, which is started if it isn't running. Tools that change the library ask the user for permission in Zotero unless they already granted it, and each such call is one step the user can undo with Edit → Undo, which moves anything added to the trash.

tools.title: Zotero status

Dates: e.g. 2020 or 2020-05-01; for isInTheLast, e.g. 7 days. collection and savedSearch: a key. annotationType: highlight, underline, note, text, image or ink. annotationColor: a hex color, as zotero_get_notes gives.

Without conditions, all items in the scope.

tools.name: zotero_list_duplicates
tools.title: List duplicate Zotero items
tools.description: List the sets of items Zotero considers duplicates, as its Duplicate Items view does: items with the same DOI or ISBN, or with similar titles, the same creators and years close together. Check that a set really is one work, e.g. not a preprint and its published version the user keeps apart, before merging it with zotero_merge_items. Each set is oldest first.

tools.name: zotero_add_items
tools.title: Add items to Zotero
tools.description:
Add items to a Zotero library, with their metadata looked up, and look for their PDFs. For BibTeX, RIS or another import format, use zotero_import. Ways to add, best first:
- identifiers: DOIs, ISBNs, arXiv IDs or PubMed IDs, or URLs that contain one (doi.org, a publisher's article page with the DOI in its URL, arxiv.org, pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov). Zotero doesn't add other web pages: the user saves those with the Zotero Connector in their browser.
- items: item JSON, for something without an identifier whose metadata you found yourself.
By default Zotero then looks for each new item's PDF or EPUB as its Find Full Text does, from the user's computer, so access through their institution works.

items.description: Item JSON in the Zotero web API format, as zotero_get_items returns, e.g. {"itemType": "report", "title": "…", "creators": [{"creatorType": "author", "firstName": "Ann", "lastName": "Lee"}], "date": "2024", "institution": "…", "url": "…"}. Only fields of the item type are accepted; zotero_list_item_types lists each type's fields and creator types. Notes and files aren't items here: add them with zotero_add_note and zotero_add_attachment.

collectionKey.description: A collection to add the items to

results.description: One per item, in the order given. An identifier can give several.

status.description: pending: Zotero is still looking up the identifier, and adds its item when it finds it.

attachments.description: The new item's attachments, e.g. the PDF Zotero found

path.description: The file, to open yourself, e.g. to see a figure. Absent if it isn't on this computer.

link.description: zotero:// link that opens the file in Zotero

fileSearch.description: For a new item without a file: whether Zotero is still looking for one

link.description: zotero:// link that shows the item in Zotero

notice.description: Present when the result is incomplete: why, and what to do next

tools.name: zotero_update_items
tools.title: Edit Zotero items
tools.description: Change items' metadata, tags and collections: set or clear fields (title, date, DOI, abstractNote and so on), replace creators, add or remove tags, and add items to or remove them from collections. To change an item's type, use zotero_change_item_types. All or nothing: one invalid change fails the call.

creators.description: Replaces all of the item's creators, in order

creatorType.description: e.g. "author" or "editor"; zotero_list_item_types lists each item type's

name.description: Instead of firstName and lastName, for an organization or a one-part name

addToCollections.description: Collection keys. An item stays in the collections it's already in.

removeFromCollections.description: Collection keys. The item stays in the library.

additionalProperties.description: Fields to set, by Zotero field name, as in item JSON (zotero_list_item_types lists each item type's), e.g. {"key": "…", "title": "…", "date": "2020-05"}. An empty string clears a field.

link.description: zotero:// link that shows the item in Zotero

tools.name: zotero_change_item_types
tools.title: Change Zotero item types
tools.description: Change items' types, e.g. from journalArticle to bookSection. Fields the new type also has keep their values. A field with a counterpart in the new type moves to it (e.g. publicationTitle becomes bookTitle; zotero_list_item_types gives each type's baseFields). Fields the new type doesn't have are removed, and the result gives their values, so you can tell the user or put them elsewhere. Use zotero_update_items afterwards to fill the new type's fields. Notes, attachments and annotations can't change type. All or nothing: one invalid change fails the call.

items.description: The items changed, with what the change did to them

link.description: zotero:// link that shows the item in Zotero

movedFields.description: Old field → the new type's field its value moved to

removedFields.description: Old field → the value it had, which the item no longer has

tools.name: zotero_merge_items
tools.title: Merge duplicate Zotero items
tools.description: Merge items that are the same work, as Zotero's merge button does: the master item keeps its own fields and gets the others' notes, files, annotations, tags, collections and related items, and the others go to the trash. Duplicate PDFs are combined, keeping the annotations of each. To use a field value from another copy, set it on the master with zotero_update_items. The items must be regular items of the same type.

masterKey.description: The item to keep, one of itemKeys. Defaults to the oldest.

link.description: zotero:// link that shows the master item in Zotero

link.description: zotero:// link that shows the collection in Zotero

tools.title: Rename or merge Zotero tags
tools.description: Rename tags on every item that has them, across a library. Renaming several to one name, which may be an existing tag, merges them. A renamed tag keeps its color. To change particular items' tags, use zotero_update_items.

tools.name: zotero_get_notes
tools.title: Get Zotero notes and annotations
tools.description: Get notes and annotations (highlights, underlines, comments and so on made in Zotero's reader). For an item, returns its notes and the annotations in its files; for an attachment, its annotations; or give note or annotation keys. Image and ink annotations (areas or drawings the user marked) have an imagePath once Zotero has rendered them; get the others' with zotero_render_annotation_images. Images in notes show as [image] in Markdown, and come in images in the same order, with their files.

tools.name: zotero_add_note
tools.title: Add a Zotero note
tools.description: Add a note, written in Markdown, under an item (a child note) or as a standalone note, optionally in a collection. Supports CommonMark with tables, ~~strikethrough~~ and TeX math: $…$ inline, and display math between lines of just $$. As when Markdown is pasted into a Zotero note, dollar signs only become math around something that looks like math (a TeX command, braces or an operator), so $x$ alone or $5 stays text. Raw HTML is shown as text, and images become links.

markdown.description: The note. Its first line becomes its title, so start with a heading.

parentItem.description: The regular item (e.g. a journal article) to add the note under

collectionKey.description: For a standalone note, a collection to put it in

link.description: zotero:// link that shows the note in Zotero

tools.name: zotero_edit_note
tools.title: Edit a Zotero note
tools.description: Add Markdown to the end of a note, or replace its content, with the same Markdown as zotero_add_note. Give the note's dateModified from zotero_get_notes: if the note changed since, e.g. because the user edited it, nothing is changed and you get it again first. Replacing works only on notes without highlights, citations or images, which Markdown can't hold; append to the others.

mode.description: replace: the Markdown becomes the whole note, and its first line the note's title

link.description: zotero:// link that shows the note in Zotero

tools.name: zotero_search_fulltext
tools.title: Search Zotero full text
tools.description: Find where words or phrases occur in the text of PDFs, EPUBs, web page snapshots and other files in a Zotero library, and get the passage around each match, with its page and a link that opens the file there. Matches words, not meaning: every word or "quoted phrase" in the query must occur in a file, ignoring case and accents, and a word also matches words it starts ("archive" matches "archives"). Only files Zotero has indexed are searched, and by default only the first 100 pages of a PDF. Files are listed by when their item was last modified, not by relevance. Use zotero_read_text to read more around a passage, and zotero_search with the fulltextContent condition to combine full text with other criteria.

query.description: Words and "quoted phrases", e.g. 'carbon "soil organic matter"'

itemKeys.description: Only these items' files, given by item or attachment keys. Not with collectionKey.

collectionKey.description: Only the files of items in this collection

includeSubcollectionItems.description: Also items in the collection's subcollections, at any depth

parentItem.description: The key of the item it belongs to

status.description: Zotero is still getting the file's text, so its passages are missing

passages.description: Passages with the most query terms first

page.description: PDF page, from 1, for zotero_read_text and links

offset.description: Character offset in a file without pages, for zotero_read_text

tools.title: Read text from a Zotero file
tools.description: Read the text of a PDF, EPUB, web page snapshot or text file in Zotero. PDFs are read by page, with the outline when Zotero has it; other files by character offset. Returns about maxChars characters per call, and nextPage or nextOffset to continue.

tools.name: zotero_find_fulltext_attachments
tools.title: Find full text in Zotero
tools.description: Look for a PDF or EPUB of items that have none, as Zotero's Find Full Text menu command does: by DOI, URL or PMCID, from open-access sources and from the publisher's site, through the user's institution where they have access. Use it for items added without files, e.g. by zotero_import. Items that already have a PDF or EPUB, or have no DOI, URL or PMCID, are skipped.

path.description: The file, to open yourself, e.g. to see a figure. Absent if it isn't on this computer.

tools.title: Generate Zotero citations
tools.description: Format items in a citation style: as one citation (with page or other locators), as a bibliography, or, with format document, all of a document's citations at once. Use format document when writing a document with several citations: give its citations in the order they appear, and get each one formatted and the bibliography, with numbering, disambiguation (Smith 2020a, 2020b) and ibid. or short forms worked out across the document. A citation formatted on its own always starts at [1] in a numeric style. For BibTeX, RIS and other export formats, use zotero_export. A style that isn't installed is installed from the Zotero Style Repository if the user allows it.

locator.description: e.g. "23" or "23-25". Not for format bibliography.

items.description: For format citation or bibliography, in citation order

citations.description: For format document: the document's citations in the order they appear, each the items cited together in one place

style.description: A style's short name, e.g. "apa", or its ID

locale.description: e.g. "en-GB". Defaults to the language Zotero is in.

citations.description: For format document, each citation in the order given

bibliography.description: For format document. Absent for a style without one.

noteStyle.description: For format document: whether the style puts citations in footnotes, one footnote per citation

tools.name: zotero_import
tools.title: Import into Zotero
tools.description: Import a file on this computer, or text, in a format Zotero imports: BibTeX, BibLaTeX, RIS, Zotero RDF, CSL JSON, MODS, EndNote XML and others. Like File → Import, the PDFs and other files a file refers to are imported too, and a file's items go into a new collection named after it unless collectionKey is given. Zotero doesn't check whether the items are already in the library.

path.description: The file's absolute path. Not with text.

collectionKey.description: A collection to add the items to

newCollection.description: Put the items in a new collection. Defaults to true for a file and false for text.

linkFiles.description: Link to the files a file refers to where they are, instead of copying them into Zotero

collectionKey.description: The collection the items went into

bestAttachment.description: What Zotero opens on double-click: its PDF, or else its oldest file or snapshot

annotationCount.description: In all its files. Absent when 0.

notice.description: Present when the result is incomplete: why, and what to do next

tools.name: zotero_export
tools.title: Export from Zotero
tools.description: Export items, a collection, or a whole library, in an export format, as text or to a new file on this computer. Formats include BibTeX, BibLaTeX, RIS, Zotero RDF, CSL JSON, CSV, MODS, EndNote XML and Markdown or HTML for notes; an unknown format gives the full list. Large exports must be written to a file.

format.description: An export format's name, e.g. "BibTeX" or "CSL JSON"

itemKeys.description: Items to export. Not with collectionKey. Without either, the whole library.

includeSubcollectionItems.description: Also the items in the collection's subcollections, at any depth. Formats that keep collections, such as Zotero RDF, then also export the subcollections.

path.description: An absolute path to write to, where nothing exists yet. Without it, the export is returned as text.

includeFiles.description: Also copy the items' files, with their annotations. path is then a new folder, with the export file inside it.

overwrite.description: Replace a file already at path. A folder, or an export with includeFiles, is never replaced.

output.description: The export, when no path was given

folder.description: The folder with the file and the items' files, for includeFiles

status.description: pending: Zotero is still writing the file

citationKeys.description: For BibTeX and BibLaTeX, of up to 500 items: the item keys of the regular items exported, each with its citation key in the export

notice.description: Present when the result is incomplete: why, and what to do next
